_read_me: Release-time obligations. Consulted by scripts/release-obligations-gate.py, which scripts/release.sh runs BEFORE any publish (dry-run included). Five ruled properties (ablative/docs tracking/ruling-release-obligations-20260809.md, commit 1369278): in the repo; on the path the act takes; the gate REFUSES rather than lists; reason_unresolved is REQUIRED while open; absence or malformed RAISES, never skips. due grammar: 'next-release' (due at any cut) or 'release:X.Y.Z' (due when the version being cut is >= X.Y.Z). An open obligation that is due REFUSES the release until it is resolved here, with the resolution stated.

obligations.title: EtsOrderedSet::new delete-vs-keep decision
obligations.origin: The citable miss: board #65 recorded 're-open EtsOrderedSet::new delete-vs-keep at the next real release' and 0.18.0 WAS that release; nothing on the release path could consult a seat's board. Ruling: ablative/docs 1369278; evidence chain verification-beamr-0180-20260809.md (docs eb55587). Subject verified live at crates/beamr/src/ets/ordered_set.rs:52 when this entry was recorded.
obligations.reason_unresolved: DECIDED 2026-08-20, lead ruling at the 0.19.3 cut (Waffles): DELETE. The constructor is #[deprecated], documented as misordering atom keys, and retained solely for out-of-tree API compatibility — the deprecation already made the design case and with_atom_table is the one correct path. Deletion is a breaking API change and cannot ride a patch, so it executes at the next breaking window: due re-anchored to release:0.20.0, which refuses that cut until the delete lands or a fresh ruling records why not. This is the decision recorded, not a date re-park.

obligations.title: Delete spawn_process raw-ip-0 scaffold entry
obligations.origin: Task #104 ruled (c): spawn_process (crates/beamr/src/scheduler/spawning.rs:78) is documented as the raw-ip-0 scaffold entry with a landing-pad death pin, and its DELETE was parked to the 0.19.0 cutter's list (landed ffbf642). Parked-to-a-release lists are exactly the class the ruling covers, so the park lives here where the cut must read it.
obligations.reason_unresolved: RULED 2026-08-20 at the 0.19.3 cut (Waffles): the delete is a breaking API change and 0.19.3 is a patch ruled on 196/196 cargo-semver-checks evidence — executing it here would force 0.20.0 across the workspace. Park re-anchored to release:0.20.0: that cut refuses until spawn_process (and its pin's scaffold caveat) is deleted or a fresh ruling keeps it. Fresh ruling per the entry's own grammar, not a date re-park.

obligations.title: Remove spawn_link_dirty alias at the next breaking release
obligations.origin: Task #38 (dirty-pool spawn-path close, main 65f499c + ladder fold d5a2709) parked the alias removal to the next breaking release. RESOLVED EXEMPLAR, recorded retroactively at pilot creation: the removal already happened at the 0.17.0 breaking window (tests/dirty_scheduler.rs:333 doc comment records it; no production spawn_link_dirty exists at the recording commit). Kept as the demonstration of the resolved shape.
obligations.resolution: spawn_link_dirty removed at the 0.17.0 breaking window; spawn_link is the one linked MFA spawn path. Verified absent from crates/*/src at pilot-creation commit; the wall test spawn_link_dirty_dispatch_is_per_entry_on_the_linked_path pins the per-entry dispatch property the alias once carried.

obligations.title: Re-run the wasm-tests leg at the aligned wasm-bindgen venue for the 0.19.4 cut
obligations.origin: The 0.19.4 gate of record (battery 9/9 at eb47329, evidence d4cd50e, gate-logs/release-0.19.4) ran on a Mac venue whose wasm-bindgen CLI is 0.2.123 against a Cargo.lock requiring 0.2.127. Project-lead ruling (Waffles, 2026-08-20 12:35Z) ACCEPTED the skewed venue for that cut only, explicitly scoped as not a precedent, on three grounds: the 0.19.4 delta is two cfg-attribute removals and a doc comment, nowhere near wasm codegen, so the leg's evidential weight for that specific change is low; the skew produced a determinate green (86 passed, rc=0), not an instrument's silence; and the leg prints its runner version as line one of battery.leg4.log, so the receipt carries its own caveat instead of laundering it. The aligned venue (host omarchy, user rocketfish, wasm-bindgen 0.2.127) was unavailable at the time: a GPU wedge with 71 uninterruptible-sleep processes, reboot held for the project lead's morning word.
obligations.reason_unresolved: The aligned re-run has not happened because the aligned venue has not returned. Resolution is one action: run the wasm-tests leg ONCE at the 0.2.127 venue and note the result here against the 0.19.4 evidence commit d4cd50e. An aligned GREEN retires the caveat and this obligation resolves with that note. An aligned RED reopens exactly one leg, not the release — 0.19.4 is published and tagged and this does not retroactively unmake it; it tells the estate the skew mattered after all, and what to do about the next cut.

obligations.title: beamr-wasm declares no readme metadata
obligations.origin: Measured at the 0.19.4 cut with `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1`: beamr, gleam-types and beamr-cli each declare license, description, repository and readme; beamr-wasm 0.9.0 declares no readme. RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md:27 requires all four on published crates. It did not block the 0.19.4 cut because beamr-wasm was already published at 0.9.0 and scripts/release.sh skips any crate whose current version is already published — so the gap rode through unpublished rather than being waived. It was deliberately NOT fixed in the 0.19.4 release commit: an unrelated manifest change inside a release commit is how a release commit stops being reviewable.
obligations.reason_unresolved: The readme key is still absent from crates/beamr-wasm/Cargo.toml. Resolve either by adding it (and confirming the referenced file exists and ships in the package), or by a recorded project-lead ruling that it waits until beamr-wasm is next actually published — that ruling is a legitimate resolution and should be stated here rather than left as a deferral. Filed as an obligation rather than remembered so it cannot silently reach the beamr-wasm bump that will refuse on it.
